summary: Modules and plugins can mark returned values deprecated with `deprecate_value` from `ansible.module_utils.datatag`, producing a warning with origin location and help text when the value is referenced.
questions: How do I deprecate a return value in my Ansible module?
How does a deprecated return value warning look?

answer_card.title: Deprecate module return values with deprecate_value
answer_card.answer_md:
Use `deprecate_value` from `ansible.module_utils.datatag` to tag a returned value. A warning appears only when a playbook references it, and shows the module and the location of the expression:

```python
from ansible.module_utils.datatag import deprecate_value

module.exit_json(
    color_name=deprecate_value(
        value="blue",
        msg="The `color_name` return value is deprecated.",
        help_text="Use `color_code` instead.",
    ),
    color_code="#0000ff",
)
```

You can also attach removal timeframes. Accessing `result.color_name` prints a `[DEPRECATION WARNING]` with the origin file, line and column plus the help text.
